title: Allow audio device switching from the task icon
line: Right-clicking an app that plays audio in the Task Manager now offers a "Play Audio Using" submenu to send its sound to another output device.
explanation: The Task Manager already finds each task's PulseAudio/PipeWire streams to show the audio indicator and the Mute item, but it never offered to choose where those streams play, so moving an app to other speakers or headphones meant opening the Audio Volume applet. The change adds a "Play Audio Using" submenu right after Mute that lists the active, non-virtual output devices (the same list the Audio Volume applet shows by default) with the device the app currently uses checked; picking one moves all of the task's streams there. The submenu only appears when the task has an audio stream and there is more than one output device.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: add a menu to choose an app's audio output device

The context menu of a task playing audio only offered muting it, so moving
an app to other speakers or headphones meant opening the audio applet. Add
a "Play Audio Using" submenu next to Mute that lists the output devices.

BUG: 445149

media.caption: Master: an app playing a tone, its task's context menu only offers Mute
With the change: "Play Audio Using" next to Mute lists Speakers, HDMI and Headphones, with Speakers (the current device) checked
After choosing Headphones the stream moved there and the submenu checks Headphones
With a single output device the submenu is hidden and the menu looks as before
